guide.title: Guide: Set up Cloudflare R2 for SAMcloud

s1.title: Create a Cloudflare account
s1.body:
Open https://dash.cloudflare.com/
Sign up or log in.
Open R2 Object Storage.

s2.title: Create a bucket
s2.body:
Click Create bucket.
Enter a name, e.g. `samcloud-shares`.
Choose Standard as the storage class.
Click Create bucket.

s3.title: Enable public access
s3.body:
Open your bucket.
Go to Settings → Public Access.
Enable the Public Development URL (r2.dev).
Copy the public URL that is shown.

s4.title: Create an API key
s4.body:
Open R2 Object Storage → Manage R2 API Tokens.
Click Create Account API token.
Use these settings: Token name: `SAMcloud`; Permissions: `Object Read & Write`; Specify bucket(s): `Apply to specific buckets only`; Bucket: select the bucket you created; TTL: `Forever`; Client IP Address Filtering: leave empty.
Click Create Account API Token.
Store the Access Key ID and the Secret Access Key safely.

s5.title: Set up automatic deletion
s5.body:
Open your bucket and go to Settings → Object Lifecycle Rules.
Create a rule named `samcloud-auto-delete`.
Choose Delete objects after 15 days.
Save and enable the rule.

s6.title: Enter the credentials in SAMcloud
s6.body:
In SAMcloud open the settings for the Cloudflare connection and enter these five values: Account ID: In R2 Object Storage (overview, not inside the bucket) on the right in the "Account Details" box – 32 characters, without https:// and without .r2.cloudflarestorage.com (it is the part before `.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` in the S3 endpoint shown after creating the token); Access Key ID: from the API token you created; Secret Access Key: from the API token you created; Bucket Name: the name of your bucket; Public URL: the public r2.dev address from step 3.
Click Test connection and save the settings.

guide.note: Important: Never share your API keys. With the public URL, files are accessible to everyone who has the link.
